note: The hosts that take a standing wall. Hand-editable. "//" is why this one, and it is the whole record of the decision. This seed is the proposal committed to the repo; the live artefacts are rule files under $ZENBORG_HOME/keel/rules/, emitted by scripts/host-block-seed.mts and installed by hand. One person's list, not a default: the domain carries no host at all, and a peer's list is their own file.

hosts.//: the one genuine hole in the old list: chess was named as a thing to curb and the second place it happens was matched by nothing. A different registrable domain, so no chess.com pattern reaches it, and a full site rather than a doorway to one.

consideredAndLeftOff.//: already covered. hostBlockRule emits *://*.<host>/* alongside the bare host, and keel's DNR projection matches requestDomains against subdomains too. A second name for a route already closed is a second place to forget.
same: a subdomain of a host, and moot besides; see linkedin.com below.

a pure redirector. Every path through it ends in a request to youtube.com, which is already refused, so adding it closes no route; it only moves where the refusal appears. It does not help on the phone either: the link hands off to the app, which never asks for either host.
the same shape for LinkedIn, and moot besides; see below.

it was here, and it was the wrong primitive. keel/docs/pain/2026-08-19-linkedin-reloads-the-feed-because-it-is-on-the-wrong-primiti.md records what a standing access-block does to a site you are already inside: the SPA is still running when the block lands, its data requests fail one at a time, its client reads each failure as a transient network error and re-mounts, and the shell keeps rendering because the asset domain is a different registrable domain. A wall a site can keep knocking on is the least reliable shape available. It gets the dwell gate instead, which the seed script emits alongside these.
